description.en: The phase drawing: the design lead draws the screens the plan's pieces change as clickable HTML mock-ups in the phase folder; another role checks them against the pieces and the design system.
description.ru: Чертёж фазы: дизайнер рисует экраны, которые меняют куски плана, кликабельными HTML-макетами в папке фазы; другая роль проверяет их по кускам и дизайн-системе.

pieces.note: the plan's pieces that change a screen: id, title, promise

folder.note: the phase folder relative to the project; mock-ups go to <folder>/design/

requirements.note: the sections UI-SPEC.md must cover, one heading each (actions, screens_states, texts, heuristics, accessibility; plus c4 and event_chain for system work)

material.note: gather MATERIAL.md before the drawing (project setting phase.draw_material = on)

nodes.prompt: Gather the material for the drawing into `<folder>/design/MATERIAL.md` — three lists with sources, no mock-up and no proposed layout: (1) patterns — existing screens and components in the repo that do a similar job, with paths; (2) references — DESIGN.md, brand, the phase's CONTEXT.md/SPEC.md/PLAN.md and any example the owner named; (3) constraints — breakpoints, accessibility, tokens, pieces that cannot change. Write nothing outside `<folder>/design/MATERIAL.md`.

Drawing rules — DESIGN.md first, then the phase's CONTEXT.md/SPEC.md/PLAN.md; every screen names its states (empty, loading, error, filled) and its breakpoints; scored on six axes: hierarchy, spacing, contrast, states, brand, motion. Motion rows follow the animator law: motion rows: animate transform and opacity only, 150–300 ms for UI feedback, ease-out entering and ease-in leaving, respect prefers-reduced-motion, no motion that blocks input, every animation has its end state drawn. Sketch rules: light and dark themes through a data-theme attribute, variants as <screen>--<variant>.html, interactivity through the shared proto script of page-prototype, plain static HTML with no build step.
If material_path arrives and is not empty, read that MATERIAL.md first (do not copy a pattern wholesale) and name MATERIAL.md in UI-SPEC.md under the patterns and constraints you used. Draw every screen the pieces in `pieces` change, as a clickable gray HTML mock-up (one file per screen) under `<folder>/design/`, following the project's DESIGN.md when there is one. Each file names the piece ids it serves. Also write `<folder>/design/UI-SPEC.md`, the drawing's contract that the verification checks: one `##` heading per section named in `requirements`, the heading text being that section's name as given (for example `## actions`, `## screens_states`), and for each screen its piece ids, its states (empty, loading, error, filled) and its breakpoints, as checkable points. Write nothing outside `<folder>/design/`.
List the files you wrote in `paths` (relative to the project), UI-SPEC.md among them. Set `feasible` false and say why in `contradiction` when a piece cannot be drawn as asked (the pieces contradict each other or the design system).

Drawing rules — DESIGN.md first, then the phase's CONTEXT.md/SPEC.md/PLAN.md; every screen names its states (empty, loading, error, filled) and its breakpoints; scored on six axes: hierarchy, spacing, contrast, states, brand, motion. Motion rows follow the animator law: motion rows: animate transform and opacity only, 150–300 ms for UI feedback, ease-out entering and ease-in leaving, respect prefers-reduced-motion, no motion that blocks input, every animation has its end state drawn. Sketch rules: light and dark themes through a data-theme attribute, variants as <screen>--<variant>.html, interactivity through the shared proto script of page-prototype, plain static HTML with no build step. Read the mock-ups in `draw.paths` and the pieces in `pieces`. You did not draw them. For each piece: is its screen there, does it show the promised behaviour, does it follow DESIGN.md, and does UI-SPEC.md list its screen's states and breakpoints and carry a heading per required section. Answer `verdict` pass or rework, with `notes` naming what to change; rework only for a missing screen, a broken promise or a design-system break, not for taste. Score the drawing 0–3 on each rubric axis in `scores` (hierarchy, spacing, contrast, states, brand, motion). If material_path arrives and is not empty, verify that UI-SPEC.md names MATERIAL.md; without material_path say nothing about MATERIAL.md.
